correctness.rationale: On the homogeneous-group manifold each majority recipient has per-edge term -d exp(-kappa d) in the A-majority snapshot (and the reversed B sign in the other); each minority recipient gains 2d toward the majority with weight one. The incidence degrees produce (-rho d q, rho d) and (-rho d, rho d q) for (a', b'), where q=exp(-kappa d). For measurable switching, the two fields are locally uniformly Lipschitz in x and measurable in time, so the restricted solution satisfying the full equations almost everywhere is the unique Caratheodory solution. The common gap obeys d'=-rho d(1+q), stays positive in finite time and is independent of chronology; opinions remain bounded and intragroup edges contribute zero. For m=(a+b)/2, the derivative is +/- w with w=rho d(1-q)/2; d decreases and d(1-exp(-kappa d)) increases strictly with d. Comparing any plus-set of measure tau to [0,tau] swaps equal masses and loses strictly unless the two sets agree almost everywhere; the reverse comparison proves the unique minimum. After both snapshots switch on, m stays fixed and d tends exponentially to zero, so the optimized quantity is eventual consensus. L_kappa'(d)=(1-q)/(2(1+q)) yields dL_kappa/dt=-w, hence the stated second difference, and Taylor expansion gives -w'(0) tau^2+O(tau^3), with exactly the positive displayed coefficient. The tau and kappa limits follow from d(t)->0 for fixed kappa and the log-cosh asymptotics, in the order stated. Intermediate consensus values are attainable by translating a contiguous plus-window from the first to the second half, continuously. An independent separated-ODE quadrature at kappa=rho=2 and tau=0.6 reproduced d(tau)=0.18700662199483575, d(2tau)=0.02003333411191537, gain 0.19960598035697165 and the alternating example 0.62492868529838253. The comparison to the prior Eq. (6) uses one term per unordered edge, consistent with its half-sum over ordered neighbors.
residual_risks: The finite checks are corroboration, not the measurable-schedule proof. The doubled LaTeX slashes at RESULT.md:76 are a typesetting typo: the preceding per-mode equations fix w unambiguously.

Equal budgets, d0>0, positive reinforcement, one snapshot at a time, exact degree balance, initial within-group homogeneity and the specified union phase matter. The strict result degenerates at kappa=0 or d0=0, outside scope.

value.rationale: The result turns a previously observed order effect into an exact global optimum with a measurable-policy strictness guarantee and closed endpoint values. Degree balance gives a reproducible criterion for when the conclusion is invariant to topology. The gain law distinguishes no first-order effect, a positive quadratic advantage and a finite long-window ceiling, useful when interpreting or designing temporal consensus computations.
residual_risks: The value is for an analytically controlled model; the theorem does not establish robustness to stochastic switching or heterogeneous initial opinions.
